selection: Seven deliberately curated research examples, not a representative or exhaustive set of complaints.

records.title: Sobhraj v. Nepal
records.citation: A/66/40 (Vol. I), Sobhraj follow-up entry, printed p. 147; Views adopted 27 July 2010
records.excerpt: shift of the burden of proof to the author (art. 14, para. 2)
records.summary: The Committee’s official report records a presumption-of-innocence violation involving the burden of proof. The entry separately discusses remedy and follow-up; the finding is not coded as release or acquittal.

records.title: Mwamba v. Zambia
records.excerpt: considers that the State party has violated article 14, paragraph 2 of the Covenant in this regard.
records.summary: The Committee found an Article 14(2) violation concerning police statements to the media affirming culpability, which the State did not dispute.

records.title: Gridin v. Russian Federation
records.citation: Human Rights Committee annual report, paragraph 579; CCPR/C/69/D/770/1997
records.excerpt: The Committee found that the authorities had failed to exercise the restraint that article 14, paragraph 2, requires.
records.summary: The official report records public guilt statements by senior law-enforcement officials, given extensive media coverage, and the Committee’s adverse finding.

records.title: Saidov v. Tajikistan
records.citation: Human Rights Committee annual report, paragraph 179; CCPR/C/81/D/964/2001, paragraph 6.6
records.excerpt: Mr. Saidov’s rights under article 14, paragraph 2, have been violated
records.summary: The official report records adverse pre-trial State-media coverage portraying the accused as criminals and an Article 14(2) violation.

records.title: Mirzakhodzhaev v. Kyrgyzstan
records.excerpt: does not disclose a violation by the State party of article 14 (1) and (2) of the Covenant.
records.summary: The majority did not find an Article 14(2) violation on the information presented about the parliamentary resolution. Dissenting opinions are identified in the decision but are not counted as the majority outcome.

records.title: Hincapié Dávila v. Colombia
records.summary: The official database classifies this communication, which includes Article 14(2), as inadmissible. It is excluded from the merits-outcome denominator.

records.title: G.B. v. Latvia
records.summary: The official database lists presumption of innocence and Article 14(2), but the decision is inadmissibility rather than a merits finding. It is excluded from the merits denominator.
